newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany cancels nearly two-thirds of Guyana's debt.
newsitem.headline: Germany cancels nearly two-thirds of Guyana's debt.

text.p: Germany said on Wednesday it had cancelled nearly two-thirds of the debts owed by Guyana which until recently was the most indebted country in the world, owing $2.1 billion.
The Finance Ministry said it had drawn up a debt conversion agreement cancelling around 17 million marks ($11.29 million) out of the 27 million marks Guyana owed Germany.

Guyana will have to pay back the remaining debt over the next 23 years. The ministry said the agreement would ensure Guyana could fulfil its obligations and no further debt conversion would be needed.

In May, Guyana won a major agreement from the Paris Club of creditor nations. It was awarded the "Naples Terms", a far-reaching debt relief deal consisting of a 67 percent stock of debt reduction with Paris Club creditors and the neighbouring island state of Trinidad and Tobago.
It is still one of Latin America's poorest nations. ($1=1.5059 Mark)
